children: Two-year agreements support vehicle registration enforcement and establish a citation-based processing fee model in a new state
SALT LAKE CITY, Sept. 29, 2026
-- OMNIQ CORP.
OTCQB:OMQS

("OMNIQ" or the "Company"), a provider of AI-based computer vision solutions, today announced that two Pennsylvania municipalities have selected Q Shield™, its Safe City platform, for vehicle registration enforcement. The agreements mark OMNIQ’s first deployments in Pennsylvania. One is with a borough in the northeast; the other is with a township in the southeast.

Q Shield™ identifies vehicles with suspended, revoked or expired registrations and, at one of the two sites, vehicles without required insurance coverage. It sends potential violations to authorized officers, who review the information and make the final enforcement decision. Officers can review activity remotely, extending coverage along busy roads without remaining stationed at a camera. The platform can also support other public safety alerts and investigations according to an agency’s configuration and authority.

The initial deployments will include a combined 18 cameras across nine intersections along corridors carrying approximately 80,000 vehicles per day, based on PennDOT traffic data. Both projects are expected to go live in 2026. OMNIQ is also in discussions with additional Pennsylvania municipalities.

Under the two-year agreements, OMNIQ will receive a processing fee associated with citations issued following agency review and authorization. The fee model creates a transaction-based recurring revenue opportunity tied to enforcement activity. Both agreements include a six-month evaluation period. Each department retains control over enforcement decisions according to its policies, staffing and applicable law.

“These agreements demonstrate the value and scalability of Q Shield for municipalities seeking to expand public-safety capabilities without proportionally increasing personnel,” said Shai Lustgarten, CEO of OMNIQ. “Pennsylvania represents a new market for the platform and a repeatable transaction-based revenue opportunity for OMNIQ. With two municipalities moving toward deployment and additional communities in discussion, we believe Q Shield can become an important part of our recurring-revenue growth strategy.”
ABOUT OMNIQ

OMNIQ CORP. uses patented and proprietary artificial intelligence to deliver machine vision image processing solutions, including data collection, real-time surveillance and monitoring for supply chain management, homeland security, public safety, traffic and parking management, and access control applications.
Our solutions help clients move people, assets and data safely and securely through airports, warehouses, schools, national borders and other environments.

Our principal solutions include hardware, software, communications, automated management services, technical services and support. Our experienced team helps customers simplify integration and deploy practical solutions across complex operating environments.
Privacy and Data Security Commitment

OMNIQ solutions are built to meet the privacy and data protection requirements of the agencies that use them. License plate data is processed and stored in a private network, and access is limited to authorized personnel at the contracting agency. Data is retained and purged according to the agency’s policy and applicable state law. OMNIQ does not sell plate data or share it with third parties for commercial purposes.
